spec.explain: From arXiv 1412.6980, this toy valley plot is illustrative: watch the step number m / sqrt(v), the bias-corrected Adam update size that stays bounded in a narrow valley.

questions.q: Set v to 1: what happens to the step? Do you expect a gradient ten times larger to make the step ten times larger?
questions.why: Tests scale invariance, the core Adam claim.

questions.q: Set m to 1: what happens to the step?
questions.why: Uses the regime value where |m| equals sqrt(v).

questions.q: Set v to 4: what happens to the step?
questions.why: Reads how larger second moment shrinks the update.

questions.q: Set m to 0.25: what happens to the step?
questions.why: Reads a small first moment value.
